request.spec:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement stays in the totals
whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on
its to-date).

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement stays in the totals
whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on
its to-date).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Holds now have dates and a person can have several of them. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 acceptance tests.

**How it works now**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V25__person_hold.sql`, adds a `person_hold` table, one row per hold, with a from-date and an optional to-date. It also drops the old `person.held` column.
- **Existing held people:** anyone already on hold gets one hold from `0001-01-01` with no end date, so their totals don't change. The old flag had no dates, so this was the only way to keep their numbers the same.
- **Server:** `POST .../people/{id}/hold` now takes `from` and `to`. A blank from-date means the sheet's today. A badly formatted date, or a to-date before the from-date, is refused and nothing is written.
  - **Audit:** a hold writes `PERSON_HELD ... name=<name> from=<date>`, followed by ROLLUP/TOTALS lines only when the hold moves the totals. `PERSON_RELEASED` is gone.
- **Live totals:** an OPEN or PENDING claim is left out only if its date falls inside one of the person's holds and no statement binds it. All other claims count. The same rule is used for the person rollup, statements, closing a period, and every total on screen.
- **Screen:** "On hold" shows yes or no depending on whether the person has any hold. Each hold is listed on its own line, and there are from/to fields and a **Hold** button that adds a hold. There's no release button any more; a hold ends on its to-date.

A statement taken on a held person also uses the new rule. If a claim inside a hold was already bound by an earlier statement, the new statement counts it and binds it again. Before, it would have been left out.

The main backend changes are in `ClaimDue.countsLive`, `Person` (new `holds` and `heldOn`, with the new `PersonHold` record), `PersonRepository`, and the hold endpoint classes. On the front end they're in `live()` in `features/claims/claims.ts` and in `features/hold/hold.slot.tsx`.
